correctness.rationale: The classical Laplacian spectrum gives the exact multipartite tree count. Forced leaves graft individually to a residual tree; the resulting inclusion probability is a product of affine-decrement factors. Each factor satisfies the discrete log-submodular two-addition inequality, with all boundary cases treated explicitly; this proves all graph sizes. A separately coded exhaustive tree enumerator and 666620 exact checks on 127 graph shapes passed. Finite tests support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The precise new invariant is the all-subset forced-leaf probability and its universal strict negative-lattice sign law; this is stronger than pairwise covariance and has a sharp complete-bipartite equality boundary. The nonuniversality of leaf correlations in uniform trees is witnessed by the positive adjacent leaf covariance 1/25 on C5. The result is a natural complete classification for every finite complete multipartite graph, not a finite arbitrary slice or isolated computation.
